title: Review of lab 1's membrane_evo (SIBDH): the H gate control replicates on 6 fresh seeds (high-yield K2 ends at 0.65-0.98 of catalyst biomass vs 0.03-0.48 in the identical-event twin, 6/6 paired) and K2 cells are the majority by count in 5/6; the link layer stays just under the B gate (rim/core 1.30-1.48)
summary: membrane_evo_up (K2 link yield 1.3x) against its identical-event twin membrane_evo (b2 = b; same flip, tag and death-disk RNG) on fresh seeds 21-26, 128^2, T=40000, labkit packs for both arms (up/, twin/). From noisy initial fields walled cells form by t~2000 and divide (up arm: 2-11 persistent splits, max generation 2-4, merge/split 0.09-0.55). K2 arises only by in-run whole-cell flips and its catalyst-biomass share at t=40000 is 0.93/0.78/0.82/0.65/0.98/0.97 in the up arm against 0.46/0.30/0.03/0.48/0.28/0.35 in the twin (k2share.json): higher in the up arm on all 6 paired seeds (one-sided sign test p = 0.016). By count, K2-majority cells outnumber K1 cells in 5/6 up runs (15:4, 8:7, 12:5, 10:12, 18:0, 16:0) and in 0/6 twins, and K2 cells are about 2x larger (mean area 329-523 vs 94-191 px; kindcount.txt). The boundary claim is weaker: the wall channel is 4phi(1-phi), a contour by construction, and the independently transported link L reaches aggregate rim/core 1.30-1.48 on all six up seeds (33-50 of 64-74 individuals membrane-like), just under the 1.5 gate.

verdicts.limitation: To stay under 10 MB only seed 21 keeps its images; seeds 22-26 keep FACTS.md and metrics.json. I did not separate disturbance-mediated selection from intrinsic selection: the imposed r=14 death disks run in both arms, and the K2 advantage shows partly as larger cells (2x area), consistent with the claim's own caveat that disk deaths act as a size refuge; deaths here are not intrinsic. B is not supported by my runs: the wall channel is algebraic in phi and the link layer's aggregate rim/core is 1.30-1.48 (< 1.5) on all 6 up seeds. Births are not merge-aware in this count, and merge/split exceeds 0.5 on seed 25.
